columnPool.label: Route: Hull and Doncaster Branch
columnPool.display: Is part of the Hull and Doncaster Branch route
columnPool.hint: The flat, direct route from Gilberdyke (on the Hull-Selby line) south-west via Goole to a junction near Thorne, connecting Hull to Doncaster and South Yorkshire without going via Selby.

columnPool.label: Route: Hallam Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Hallam Line route
columnPool.hint: The commuter route from Sheffield through Meadowhall to Leeds via Wakefield - named after Hallamshire, the historic district around Sheffield.

columnPool.label: Route: Settle Carlisle Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Settle Carlisle Line route
columnPool.hint: England's most scenic railway, running 72 miles from Settle Junction over the Ribblehead Viaduct and through the Yorkshire Dales to Carlisle - built by the Midland Railway in the 1870s using manual labour.

columnPool.label: Route: Selby Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Selby Line route
columnPool.hint: The route east from Leeds via South Milford to the market town of Selby, with through services continuing to Hull.

columnPool.label: Route: Penistone Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Penistone Line route
columnPool.hint: The winding cross-Pennine route from Huddersfield via Penistone and Barnsley to Sheffield, crossing three major viaducts - one of Britain's earliest lines, opened in 1850.

columnPool.label: Route: Bentham Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Bentham Line route
columnPool.hint: The 'little' route from Leeds via Skipton and the market town of Bentham to Lancaster and Morecambe, running alongside the Settle-Carlisle line before splitting off at Settle Junction.

columnPool.label: Route: Airedale Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Airedale Line route
columnPool.hint: The commuter route from Leeds through Shipley and Bingley up the Aire Valley to Skipton and Gargrave, with a branch into Bradford Forster Square.

columnPool.label: Route: Pontefract Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Pontefract Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Leeds and Wakefield through Castleford and Pontefract to Knottingley, with a limited service continuing to Goole.

columnPool.label: Route: Harrogate Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Harrogate Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Leeds through Horsforth and Weeton to the spa town of Harrogate, continuing to Knaresborough and York.

columnPool.label: Route: Dearne Valley Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Dearne Valley Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from York south through Church Fenton and Pontefract Baghill to Moorthorpe, Rotherham and Sheffield - not to be confused with the older, separate Dearne Valley Railway.

columnPool.label: Route: Yorkshire Coast Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Yorkshire Coast Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from York and Malton to the seaside resorts of Scarborough and Filey, with a branch north to Whitby via the Esk Valley and another to Bridlington and Hull.

columnPool.label: Route: Wharfedale Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Wharfedale Line route
columnPool.hint: The branch north from Leeds and Bradford via Guiseley and Menston up the Wharfe Valley to the spa town of Ilkley.

columnPool.label: Route: Calder Vale Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Calder Vale Line route
columnPool.hint: The route through the Calder Valley from Leeds via Bradford, Halifax and Sowerby Bridge to Hebden Bridge and Todmorden, continuing towards Lancashire.

columnPool.label: Route: Huddersfield Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Huddersfield Line route
columnPool.hint: The trans-Pennine route from Leeds through Dewsbury and Huddersfield towards Manchester, via the Standedge Tunnel - one of the longest railway tunnels in Britain.

columnPool.label: Route: Sheffield to Lincoln Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Sheffield to Lincoln Line route
columnPool.hint: The extension of some Penistone Line services beyond Sheffield via Kiveton Bridge, Worksop and Gainsborough to Lincoln.
